correctness.rationale: The proof uses the independent directed-attachment representation of the stationary Moran forest (Bienvenu–Duchamps–Foutel-Rodier Prop. 2.1) up to relabeling: K=sum 1_{U_j>j}, total degree D_j=1-B_j+C_j and zero-child status 1_{C_j=0}. I independently enumerated all (n-1)^(n-1) attachment assignments for n=2,...,7 in exact rational arithmetic; the closed binomial-difference covariance for every degree agrees, as does Z. For n=4 the degree-one covariance is -2/27 and terminal covariance 2/9. The sign argument uses unimodality of binomial probabilities with success probability 1/(n-1); the degree-one formula factors into a sum of strictly negative terms except n=3 equality. The asymptotic constants follow by dominated Riemann sums of exact formulas, not finite extrapolation. Boundary n=2 and out-of-range degrees are handled.

originality.rationale: Bienvenu–Duchamps–Foutel-Rodier characterize marginal component counts and vertex degrees under the stationary Moran law, providing the sampler but not joint component/degree-histogram covariance or the contrast with zero-outdegree. Published random recursive tree and uniform recursive forest results use distinct distributions and cannot dominate this joint statement. A Resultary search showed no exact stationary Moran covariance match.
residual_risks: The 1994 full paper could not be inspected; priority uncertainty remains but its distribution is distinct.
No statement about stochastic association or a full joint CLT is established.

value.rationale: An exact all-degree sign diagram and the counterintuitive distinction between low undirected degree and terminal child count are natural structural statistics of a canonical stationary random forest. The explicit finite-size covariance row and nonzero opposite-sign limits are useful beyond routine marginal laws.
